title: Engineer's Notes
raw_text:
<font face='$HandwrittenFont' size='15'>Adgran insists, but I don't know why, we're perfectly capable of launching the ship by ourselves. Though, orders are orders.
Initial surveys of the engine and its relevant mechanisms proved enlightening. Previously, we had speculated that Dwemeri aetherships operated similar to previous studied modes of aetherjumping, such as Vehkship's primitive ASSN, though built for longer range slingshots. What we failed to realize, is that the dwemer prefer to find alternatives to magic, even for such magics as advanced as mnemolic arrays and spore hashtables. We had also previously assumed that aetherium served to propel the ship, again, failing to realize the bias against magic. In truth, Aetherium serves not as the power source for travel, but the catalyst for it. With a sufficient amount of aetherium, tonal resonators contained in blocks A154 and A155 are capable of discerning origin-times, which are then stored in the memoryspores above. From here, a pastline is capable of being formed, while primal (and for longer jumps, secondary) bellturners wrinkle or bend the line towards the destination. From here, the memospores, added by what is believed to be a primitive story array, reverts the Aetherium to the location, with the ship in tow. However, while revolutionary and efficient (especially in comparison to our own engines, we're still on 6th dimensional Magnus slingshots!), there is a significant limitation. Both planefall and leaving orbit requires a traditional form of transportation, as the line-variation pattern can too great while grounded. As such, the ship must be physically pushed off world, whether by rocket or magical lift. This explains the enormous fuel tanks down on the lower decks, while not necessary for travel in the void, it is necessary for landings and departures. As it stands, refueling the ship is not a difficult task, as the pumps are in working order, and the main control can be found in the Tower of Uplifting. What presents a difficult task is creating an aetherium plate to let the ship travel. Without the aid of a Tonal Architect, the aetherions do provide a pure enough form to be usable, though I've noted that the original plate has been broken into three pieces, as we have already recovered one piece of it. It is possible therefore, that one might be able to reforge the old one.
</font>

title: Engineer's Notes
raw_text:
<font face='$HandwrittenFont' size='15'>While the bridge is currently inoperative, the underdeck provided a good view of how the piloting mechanisms work. 
Two components are provided for travel, the navigation system, and the actual switch for travel. Provided both are online, and the ship has left the orbit, one may select a destination from the navigation system, then flip the switch to travel to the aforementioned destination. Again, this is provided that all systems are online. As it stands however, navigation appears to be damaged, though this may be easy to fix, I expect that it's just a loose sight-conduit, or something similar, probably down in the maintenance tunnels. Unfortunately, the door to the tunnels appears to be sealed. I suspect it will only open once the ship has left orbit.
</font>

title: Adgrand's Report
raw_text:
<font face="$HandwrittenFont">To the Lord High Archcanon and His Eternity, the Pearlescent Helmsman,

We have reached the ship, though the cost of life may have been too great. I myself have sustained irreparable injuries, and of the original party, only myself and two others, both engineers, remain-
Damn the report! You there! Yes you, the one reading this! I don't know how long it's been or how long it will be, but you must listen to me! You stand, hopefully, in the bay of an aethership, the very last aethership. Above all else, this ship MUST BE LAUNCHED. We are chronographers, those that prepare events to happen, saving lives in the process. Now understand this, in the 7th Era, in orbit above Baar Dan, a battle between a rogue faction of Ideal Masters and Histian mercenaries will take place. While the Masters will initially have the upper hand, the Hist will turn the tide of battle using a powerful recovered dwemer aethership floating nearby. This is that ship. Above all else, if this ship does not launch, then it will not be present at that battle, the integrity of the event will not be preserved, and the Ideal Masters will win. If this happens, the following months will see the deaths of countless people in their onslaught against existence. This must not happen.
We sought to launch it ourselves, but the centurions have proven too much for us. Perhaps your survival indicates that you, indeed, are capable of succeeding where we have failed. My wounds are too great, and I fear that when I die, my engineers shall soon follow. As such, I have instructed them to leave behind as many notes as possible, to assist you in your endeavors. If you wish for a reward, fine, the ship will be yours to command, as you will no doubt have died by the time of the 7th era, feel free to loot anything else you find, the dead care not for possessions. All I ask is, again, that you launch the ship and prevent a horrible tragedy from occurring.
For the sake of the unborn millions and myself, I thank you.
Century Adgran
Chief Chronographer of the Gyroship Aytz-Makan
</font>

Your loyal part in the machine,
Century Adgran

title: Chronography, Volume 1
raw_text:
[pagebreak]

Chronography, Volume 1 By Monden Marvayn

[pagebreak]

Knowledge and the knowledge of that knowledge comes and goes. What one generation knows for a fact the next only knows as myth. Such is not the case with the Skyriders, better known to me and my fellow Dunmer scholars as the Pearlescent Chronographers. While those not from Morrowind may not recognize the name, natives will no doubt at this point be familiar with who I speak of. To the uninitiated, I say welcome, and let me answer both yours and my fellow kinsmen lingering questions on the mysterious clockwork gift-givers. History: What we first knew of the Chronographers came from our encounters with them. Or perhaps Encounters, for the shows they so performed no doubt deserve a capital letter. And while incredible, mind-shattering, and all-around unusual, the Chronographers always behaved the same in a situation. Dunmer, in their time of need, would find fleets of whirling dwemer contraptions, or mechanical creatures descending from the sky, upon which rode mystics, dressed in metal, with fire-red eyes and limbs of steel. These visitors would impart upon the needy contraptions and physical riddles, which in time would reveal their purpose, always benevolent and helpful. It was only after careful studying, and a chance meeting an interview with one of these Chronographers, that we learned the truth. The Chronographers Pious dunmer may know of the Mystery of Morrowind, otherwise known as Sotha Sil, Seht, or the Clockwork King. A mystic, an engineer, and former god of the Dunmer people, Sotha Sil retreated into his mysterious Clockwork City many years ago, where he was killed by his friend and fellow Tribunal member, Almalexia. What many do not know however, is what happened following this. You see, his city was not merely a workshop, but a sprawling metropolis. And in this metropolis live fabricants, mer-machines, living automatons who worked and loved in the city. But with their king and creator dead, the fabricants were faced with a decision. Stay in their home, no doubt soon to crumble without its creator to guide it, or leave? While a schism may have divided other such people, the fabricants were unanimously swayed by a group known as the Armour of Oscillating Quartz (see volume 3: origins). This group swayed the city into following them aboard a fleet of mysterious "helicarriers" (see volume 2: technology) from which they sailed out of the city, no doubt seeking a new purpose in their lives, for what are machines without purpose?

title: Chronography, Volume 2
raw_text:
[pagebreak]

Chronography, Volume 2 By Monden Marvayn

[pagebreak]

Technology: Perhaps the most observable instances of Chronographer technology are their ships, deemed 'helicarriers' by the masses. Drawing inspiration from Merethic era mananauts, these enormous floating ships descend upon villages. I can't fully say what capabilities these ships truly possess, but the speed at which they move suggests some otherworldly engineering we can barely comprehend. While not regularly armed, in the few cases where fabricants have fought, they have favored mysterious projectile weapons, referred to in obscure dwemer texts as "harquebus" or "harquebuses". Again, little is known about these contraptions. Certain people have also noted that many events with the Chronographers happen in a non-linear fashion. Many talk of remembering events before they happen, or waking up several days ago after having fallen asleep a week from then. Observed technologies confirm that the Chronographers are capable of time-shifts and timestops, and their incredible technology may come from the fact that they are capable of traveling to the far future, gaining access to things we haven't even conceived of yet. The final piece of their creation are Imperfections, a general term used by them to refer to the strange puzzles they grant those in need. These Imperfections cannot be classified, as each one seems to function differently. One account told of how his perfection changed into a memory speak-box, and over time taught him the ways of a different man, eventually allowing him to win over the woman of his dreams. Others have become showers of gold, a sword in the right place. Whatever their purpose, these Imperfections all have the end goal of being helpful, which leads me to my next section Purpose: We forget at times that the Chronographers are machines, though aware and intelligent. To them, purpose, not living, is what drives them. But what purpose do they have you ask? It took many years to figure out, but accounts and evidence overwhelmingly point to what I will refer to, and what has been referred, as integrity preservation. As time-travelers, the Chronographers have knowledge of events before they happen. But rather than try to take advantage of these, they are content with a more noble goal, and try to prevent such events from NOT happening. By dispensing their gifts to strangers, they lightly nudge events, preserving what they no doubt believe is the integrity of time. For example, a gift given to a starving man may in time, feed him, and allow him to get back on his feet. In time, that man would lead armies, or change events significantly. It is hard to say what the end goals of this preservation is, but for now, those who receive a gift from the Chronographers should consider themselves lucky, for they have a part to play in a larger affair, and a destiny awaiting them.

Rather than let his comrades die, it is said that Sotha Sil reforged them into automatons of crystal. These twelve hundred saints, as history notes, became known as the Armour of Oscillating Quartz, the same faction that swayed the fabricants to leave Sotha Sil. It is believed that they believe that their reforging was done for a specific purpose, though one that would take years to come to fruition. No doubt this fueled their philosophies when convincing the fabricants to become the Chronographers as we know them now.

title: Adgran's Notes
raw_text:
<font face='$HandwrittenFont' size='15'>Initial deconstruction yields nothing, suspected that therefore the Centurions encountered are using some other form for power, Decade Salas is currently investigating animunculi and power sources.
UPDATE: Salas' suspicions were correct! While most animunculi have an ATHM level of around fifteen, the current centurions are estimated to have a level of around 140-200. This would require an extensive power source, rich in either magicka or something similar, though unfortunately we haven't acquired any sort of intact power source to find out what that would be.
</font>

title: Adgran's Notes
raw_text:
<font face='$HandwrittenFont' size='15'>Some of the lower ranks had suspicions of Aetherium, and while I agreed at first, now we have absolute confirmation. We managed to take one of these centurions intact, and amazing, the standard power core was replaced with starmetal. These automatons are Aetherium powered! It explains a lot, but perhaps suggests something deeper. As we know, the Skyrim dwemer tore each other to pieces over Aetherium, and such large amounts of it can only suggest something deeper. Rathamaz is probably not heavily defended against intruders, but against other dwemer, seeking the centurions themselves!
Not only that, but given aetherships nature, the centurions could be dismantled and used as a backup source of fuel. With all their uses, my subordinates have taken to calling them Aetherions.
</font>

title: Minute Masecun's Journal
raw_text:
<font face='$HandwrittenFont' size='15'>I can't be the only one who smells it, can I? This place reeks of aetherial tampering. I'm not scholar, but me the other lads are assuming that anything with this much smell would no doubt mean one thing, Aetherium. Star-metal. Makes sense that the dwarves might use it to power their ships, but we're miles from the launchpad. So where's the damned Aetherium?
</font>
